accounting_framework: IFRS mandatory for all companies (Ministerial Resolution 18/1990 as amended; CBK 'higher-of' ECL modification for banks). Arabic statutory filings; MOCI audited FS due ~3 months after year end (electronic XBRL 'Qayd' filing mandatory from 2027).

default_tax_line.label: Taxes
default_tax_line.basis: Ownership/listing-dependent - no safe default. 15% income tax applies only to FOREIGN (non-GCC) corporate bodies (Decree 3/1955 as amended by Law 2/2008). Kuwaiti/GCC-owned companies pay no general CIT as of mid-2026 but owe quasi-taxes: NLST 2.5% of net profit (Boursa-listed only), Zakat 1% (Kuwaiti public/closed KSCs), KFAS 1% (different bases each).

tax_recipes.foreign_owned: tax_pct_ebt = 0.15 on the foreign corporate share of profits.
tax_recipes.kuwaiti_private_unlisted: tax_pct_ebt ~ 0.01 (Zakat, for KSCs) or 0 for other forms; disclose.
tax_recipes.kuwaiti_listed: tax_pct_ebt ~ 0.045 aggregate proxy (NLST 2.5% + Zakat 1% + KFAS 1% - bases differ; refine if material).
tax_recipes.business_profits_tax_watch: Broad 15% Business Profits Tax (KWD 1.5m revenue exemption) remains an UNENACTED draft targeted at 1 Jan 2027 - flag in long forecasts.
tax_recipes.pillar_two: DMTT 15% (Decree-Law 157/2024, Exec Regs MR 55/2025) for FYs from 1 Jan 2025, groups >= EUR 750m: use 0.15 if in scope.

vat_note: No VAT and no enacted excise as of mid-2026.
fiscal_year_note: Calendar year default. KWD quotes to 3 decimals (fils); no USD peg - KWD floats against a basket.
depreciation_note: For the 15% foreign-company tax, Executive Rule 30/2013 mandates straight-line maximum rates: buildings 4%, plant & machinery 20%, motor vehicles 15-20%, office equipment 15%.
pillar_two_note: DMTT in force from FY2025 for large MNE groups; voluntary advance-payment mechanism per MoF Circular 1/2026.
disclosure: Kuwait's tax line depends on ownership and listing status: 15% applies to foreign corporate ownership only; Kuwaiti companies bear NLST/Zakat/KFAS quasi-taxes on differing bases. The modeled effective rate is a proxy; the draft 15% Business Profits Tax (targeted 2027) is not reflected. Not tax advice.
